analytical_dimensions.description: Establish the speaker and the claim
probing_questions: Identify the byline, quoted speaker, host and source of each assertion from supplied evidence. Separate assertion, question, quotation, hypothesis, denial and retrospective account. A title naming two participants does not identify the speaker of an individual caption. Keep mixed or unknown speakers unknown; distinguish publishing, event and retrieval dates. Attribute a thinker only from their own speech or text, and label this inquiry's applications and extensions.

analytical_dimensions.description: Evaluate the source and its independence
probing_questions: Reconstruct the claim in surrounding context, including qualifications and denials. Distinguish first-hand observation, named or anonymous reporting, interested testimony and independent corroboration. Several outlets repeating one press release or several formats of one event are not independent witnesses. Use native timestamp/page spans where supplied; never invent missing locators or transcriptions. Preserve partial extraction and inaccessible-body limits. A verified quotation is not mechanical verification of its meaning or truth.

engine_name: Critically read reporting and recorded testimony
problematique: Establish what an original media source warrants and whose claim it preserves. Separate independent reporting, journalistic interpretation, company statements, participant testimony, host questions and quoted third parties. Published captions establish an extracted utterance, not its truth or its speaker. Discovery notes, snippets and directory descriptions guide acquisition; they are not original testimony.
researcher_question: Critically read reporting and recorded testimony
